purpose: Closes the allowlist blind spot that this session introduced in the first matrix: the collector only accepted devicePixelRatio 1 and 2, so fractional device pixel ratios (the common 1.25/1.5 laptops) and DPR 3 were structurally untestable. tools/verify/spark-pixel-parity.cjs and tools/debug/probes/spark-pixel-parity/frame.js now share the allowlist {1, 1.25, 1.375, 1.5, 2, 3} and both reject a CSS size whose device dimensions are not integers or exceed 1024, so the sweep cannot silently paper over double-rounding. The first three windows of this file were collected when the allowlist was still {1, 1.5, 2, 3}; the 1.25/1.375 tiers were added afterwards and the last three windows come from that second widening.
strictRule: Unchanged: every RGBA8 channel byte difference must be 0, both sides non-empty, each side stable against its own repeat, zero JS + drained GL errors, identical context attributes and unmasked renderer inside one engine, source/asset digest unchanged during the run, negative control must move pixels. No tolerance, no masks.
noteOnPredecessorEvidence: The 60-row matrix file was collected BEFORE this harness change, so its rows bind the pre-change collector. Nothing in that file is invalidated: the engine/SDK target path and the comparator are untouched, and the fractional windows here re-run the same four cases through the widened allowlist.
notClaimed: Not a cross-GPU/device generalisation: evidence binds to the three browser builds and this machine GPU listed in windows[].engines and .gpu.
Not release READY: the spark-rs crate-level licence disposition is still `pending` in docs/license-decisions.json.

The browser context deviceScaleFactor is set to the requested DPR, but pixels() compares the default framebuffer read back over canvas.width/height; a mismatch between the page-reported scale and the canvas-derived scale is still not covered.

The 1.25 and 1.375 tiers are now in the shared allowlist, but the set is still a deliberate finite list, not a general proof: any other ratio (0.75, 1.75, 2.5, …) remains untested and would be rejected by the collector until added and shown to give integer device pixels.

Each windows[].sourceFreeze.files/aggregateSha256 is the digest taken BEFORE that window ran, so it identifies the state the window exercised; it is not a proof that later windows or later commits share that state. In particular the first three windows were collected against the pre-widening collector fingerprints.
